mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes S 350d or S 400d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM656 engine for the S 350d or S 400d costs £2,800-£4,900 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,200-£2,500 depending on complexity - the inline-six requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of EGR failure on a Mercedes S 350d or S 400d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Reduced performance, increased fuel consumption, rough idling and dashboard warning lights are the classic warning signs on the OM656 engine. The EGR valve and cooler can become clogged with soot over time.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes S 350d or S 400d engine (OM656) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM656 is considered 'pretty reliable' by specialists. However, it has known issues: vacuum pump problems in the 25,000-40,000 mile range, camshaft and rocker wear around 100,000 miles, and EGR system clogging. With these addressed, the engine is proving durable.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes S 350d and S 400d engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM656 is too new for definitive long-term data, but with regular maintenance and proactive attention to known issues, 150,000+ miles is achievable. Some early failures have been reported, but overall reliability is improving.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes S 350d or S 400d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the S-Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major electrical faults. A rebuilt OM656 costs £2,800-£4,900 - far less than replacing a £25,000-£60,000 vehicle. The S-Class's strong residual values make engine replacement financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes S 350d or S 400d need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies low-SAPS oil meeting MB 229.52 - typically 5W-30. The OM656 inline-six requires approximately 8.5 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 350d/400d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The S 350d and S 400d launched with the facelift W222 generation in 2017, powered by the all-new OM656 3.0-litre inline-six diesel - the most powerful series-production car diesel engine ever offered by Mercedes-Benz. The OM656 replaced the OM642 V6 diesel with a straight-six architecture featuring stepped-bore combustion, twin sequential turbochargers, and advanced emissions technology. The S 400d, with 340hp and 700Nm of torque, set a new benchmark for diesel performance in a luxury saloon. Both variants continued into the W223 generation, representing the pinnacle of Mercedes diesel engineering.

milestones.description: W223 generation launch; OM656 continues with refinements
present - OM656 continues as the flagship diesel for S-Class

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz S Class 350d and 400d is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from OM656 EGR cooler cracking to vacuum pump and camshaft rocker wear issues.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 350d/400d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The OM656 inline-six diesel is Mercedes' most advanced diesel engine, delivering exceptional performance and refinement. However, as with any complex modern diesel, it has well-documented issues that can lead to significant repair costs. EGR system clogging, vacuum pump failures, and camshaft wear are the most commonly reported problems. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: OM656 EGR System Clogging & Cooler Issues
problems.h4: OM656 EGR System Clogging & Cooler Issues - The Modern Diesel's Emissions Challenge
problems.rootCause: The OM656 features both cooled low-pressure and high-pressure EGR systems. Carbon deposits can accumulate over time, leading to reduced performance, increased emissions, and warning lights on the dashboard. The EGR valve and cooler are prone to clogging with soot and combustion by-products.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR valve and cooler passages, system recalibration
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early with mild symptoms

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler unit, clean intake passages, reset adaptations
repairOptions.longevity: If cleaning does not resolve the issue

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with new EGR components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If EGR failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2017-present S 350d or S 400d is worth approximately £25,000-£60,000 depending on mileage and condition. The S-Class flagship retains strong residual values - replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: EGR clogging on the OM656 is primarily an emissions-system maintenance issue. If caught early, cleaning the EGR system at a specialist is a cost-effective solution. If the EGR cooler requires replacement, specialist pricing of £750-£1,200 is significantly lower than dealer rates. Regular use of quality diesel and occasional motorway driving can help prevent carbon buildup.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM656 Mercedes S 350d/400d engine prices

problems.h4: OM656 Vacuum Pump Failure - The Coolant Leak Recall Issue
problems.rootCause: A leak may develop between the coolant pump and the vacuum circuit, allowing coolant to enter the vacuum system. This can affect components and lead to an increase in temperature, potentially causing a fire. Mercedes recalled over 800,000 vehicles worldwide with OM654 and OM656 diesel engines over this issue.

repairOptions.tier: Recall Remedy - Coolant pump vacuum leak repair
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace coolant pump switch valve, inspect vacuum system
repairOptions.longevity: Check your VIN for outstanding recall status

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect vacuum system, replace affected components
repairOptions.longevity: If recall has been performed but symptoms persist

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with updated coolant pump and vacuum components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If coolant ingress has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical S 350d/400d is worth £25,000-£60,000.
problems.recommendation: If your S 350d or S 400d is subject to the coolant pump vacuum leak recall, have the work performed at a Mercedes dealer free of charge. If symptoms persist or the recall doesn't apply, specialist inspection is essential. On an S-Class worth £25,000-£60,000, preventative attention to this issue is always the better investment.

problems.h4: OM656 Camshaft & Rocker Wear - The High-Mileage Inline-Six Concern
problems.rootCause: OM654 and OM656 engines can suffer from camshaft and rocker wear, typically around 100,000 miles, sometimes less. Cam rocker wear can manifest as a popping sound from the intake. This is a relatively expensive repair job requiring specialist attention.

problems.h4: OM656 AdBlue System Failure - The SCR Countdown Warning
problems.rootCause: The AdBlue dosing system can suffer from pump failure or injector clogging due to urea crystallisation. Fault codes P203B31 (AdBlue fill level sensor) and P206B31 (AdBlue concentration sensor) can trigger countdown warnings and eventual engine start prevention.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic scan of SCR system, tank, dosing module, NOx sensors
repairOptions.longevity: First step - confirms which component has failed

repairOptions.longevity: If AdBlue failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: AdBlue faults are primarily emission-system issues, not core mechanical failures. If your S 350d or S 400d displays a countdown warning, have the SCR system inspected immediately. Specialist AdBlue injector or pump replacement at £350-£800 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. On an S-Class worth £25,000-£60,000, preventative attention is always the better investment.
